data.name: Hasab
data.gender_notes: Hasab is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'h-s-b', meaning 'to give' or 'to give as a gift'. In Islamic tradition, Hasab refers to the balance that Allah will use to weigh the deeds of each person on the Day of Judgment. The name Hasab carries the meaning “Gift, Reward” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hasab usually hope their child will grow to embody gift, reward and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes the balance and justice of Allah.
data.etymology: Hasab belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gift, Reward.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hasab total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: حساب
in_arabic.meaning: الحساب: الحساب هو العلاج لما تودعه السماء في أجر العبد
in_arabic.long_meaning: الحساب، هو العلاج لما تودعه السماء في أجر العبد، ومعناه إحصاء الأمور، وإعطاء العبد ما يستحقه من أجر، وموجودة في القرآن الكريم في سورة الزلزلة الآية 18، وهو من أقدم المصطلحات المستخدمة في الإسلام، وقد كان يستخدم في الحسابات المالية والاقتصادية قبل الإسلام، وينقسم الحساب إلى قسمين، الأول هو الحساب بين الله وبين عباده، والثاني هو الحساب بين العبد وبين نفسه، وهو من أهم مبادئ الإسلام، ويعتبر الحساب العادل والمنصف هو الحساب الذي يوازن بين حقوق كل فرد وعليه

data.spiritual_significance: The concept of Hasab holds great spiritual significance in Islamic beliefs, as it represents the ultimate judgment and determination of a person's fate in the hereafter. Believers hold that their deeds, good or bad, will be weighed on the Day of Judgment, and that the balance of good deeds will ensure entry into paradise and eternal happiness, while the weight of bad deeds will result in eternal punishment in the fire of Hell. This notion instills a deep sense of responsibility and fear of accountability, motivating the faithful to engage in daily acts of virtuous behavior and maintain a strong spiritual connection to Allah.
